purpose: A FileDropzone is the target a user drags files from the operating system onto. It owns the drag lifecycle (only drags carrying `Files` count), the `accept` / `multiple` filtering, and the idle/active look, and it hands the result back as two activation events: `drop` with the accepted files, `reject` with the files it filtered out. It holds no value and renders no file list. The list, upload progress and validation messages belong to the consumer (typically a `Field` around this component, whose `Field.Description` / `Field.Error` carry the messages). `kind` covers the two places a drop target lives: - **`inline`**: a dashed region that is always visible (icon, title, description, plus a default slot for the "Browse files" action the consumer composes). It switches to the active look while files are dragged over it. This is the Cloudscape FileDropzone / Cloudflare Pages "Upload assets" shape. - **`overlay`**: invisible at rest. When files are dragged into the window it fades in over its nearest positioned ancestor (`absolute inset-0`), and it fades out on window drag-leave, drop or `Escape`. This is the Vercel "drag and drop a folder to deploy" shape, and it replaces the sample app's page-level `ProjectDropZone` and the drop target in the `Templates/Platform/States/ProjectIntake` story. The drop target itself is pointer-only. It is never a keyboard control. The keyboard (and screen-reader) path to the same outcome is a real button the consumer puts in the default slot (`inline`), or elsewhere on the page (`overlay`).
useWhen: A form or settings surface accepts one or more files and should also accept them by drag (`kind="inline"` with a Browse button in the slot).
A whole page or card should accept a project, folder contents or assets dropped anywhere on it, with no permanent drop region taking up space (`kind="overlay"` inside a `relative` container).
The consumer needs the accepted and rejected files separated by an `accept` filter before it uploads anything.
avoidWhen: Picking files by keyboard or click only, with no drag affordance → a `button` that opens a native file input is enough.
Showing the chosen files, their progress or their errors → render them yourself with `progress`, `message` or `helper-text`. The dropzone renders none of these.
Dragging items inside the page (reordering rows, moving cards) → this component only reacts to OS drags that carry `Files`. In-page drag and drop is out of scope.
A static "nothing here yet" panel with no drop behavior → use `empty-state`.
related: button`: the "Browse files" action composed into the default slot. It is the keyboard path to the same outcome as a drop.
empty-state`: a no-data panel. Compose a FileDropzone inside or beside it when the empty state's call to action is "upload".
progress`: the consumer renders per-file progress after `drop`. The dropzone does not track uploads.
toast`: confirms the result of a drop or reports rejected files to everyone, including users who never see the drag.
card`: a positioned container (`class="relative"`) that hosts an `overlay` dropzone.
bestPractices: Always give the user a non-drag path. In `inline`, put a `Button` in the default slot that opens a native `<input type="file">`. In `overlay`, keep an upload button somewhere on the page. The drop target is pointer-only by design.
Pass the same `accept` string to the dropzone and to the native input behind your Browse button, so both paths filter the same way.
Handle `reject`. Tell the user which files were skipped and why (e.g. a `toast` naming the files and the accepted types). A silent rejection reads as a broken drop.
Announce the outcome of a drop yourself (a toast, or a live region on your file list). The dropzone does not announce drag states (see Accessibility).

Render one `overlay` dropzone per positioned container, and make the container `relative`. Without a positioned ancestor the overlay covers the nearest positioned element up the tree, which may be the whole page.
Place the `overlay` dropzone as the last child of its container, so it paints above the container's other positioned content (see Theme gaps).
When the consumer's own flow is busy (an upload in progress), set `disabled` and disable the Browse button too.
Put the accepted types and limits in `description` ("PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB"). The title is the instruction, the description is the constraint.
